subject: Re: FinCoBank evals setup — recommended models & dataset/metrics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@fincobank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinCoBank — post-demo recap & next steps (evals)

Alex — great to meet yesterday. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can run a customer-specific eval on Redwood and validate model fit:

TL;DR
- Goal: Evaluate model quality on FinCoBank customer support prompts (intent classification + response quality) and baseline cost/latency on Redwood Dedicated.
- Ask from you: share a representative sample dataset (CSV) with prompt/context rows + expected labels/examples; confirm success criteria for quality.
- Redwood will: provision an eval run (we use the redwood_eval_template.md) with recommended model candidates, scoring scripts, and a results dashboard link.

Recommended models (initial shortlist):
- Llama-2-13B (quantized) — good balance of cost and quality for conversational classification tasks.
- RedGem-7B-v2 — lower cost sibling, good for intent classification and scale.
- RedGem-34B (fp16) — if you need higher response quality/regression-sensitive outputs.

Proposed evaluation plan:
1) You upload a CSV with columns: id, user_message, context (optional), expected_label, expected_response (optional).
2) We'll run three model variants across the dataset with deterministic seeds where applicable.
3) Metrics: intent accuracy, response ROUGE/EM/F1 (where relevant), and a human-sampled precision review for N=200.
4) Cost/latency: tokens per request, p95 latency on Dedicated pool.

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.md (template for dataset + scoring), example CSV stub attached.

Next steps: can you share the dataset and confirm whether the primary success metric should be intent accuracy >= 92% or whether you prefer response-level F1? If you want, we can also run a bias/regression check against your production prompts.

Thanks — happy to set up a quick 20-min sync if you'd like to walk through the template.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Sent from my calendar (available 10/16 10–12 PDT)

Thanks Marissa — really clear, appreciate the recap. A couple of clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset: we'll share a 2k-row sample CSV by EOD 10/16. It will include id, user_message, intent_label, and a short canonical_response for about 30% of rows. Is the CSV layout in redwood_eval_template.md the correct canonical format?
2) Success metric: intent accuracy is primary — target 92% baseline, but we'd like to prioritize reducing false positives on escalation intents (safety-critical).
3) Security: Does Redwood isolate eval data on Dedicated instances and purge dataset after runs? We need to include this in procurement docs.

Also looping Priya (PM) who will own the dataset export. Happy to do the 20-min sync if Neha can join for infra/config questions.

— Alex

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Miller <alex.miller@fincobank.com>, Priya Das <priya.das@fincobank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 08:37:22 -0700
Subject: Re: FinCoBank — post-demo recap & next steps (evals)

Alex/Priya — thanks for the quick reply. Happy to run the sync and answer infra + security questions. A few specifics to address your asks and to make the eval run reproducible:

Dataset format (redwood_eval_template.md attached):
- Required columns: id, user_message, context, expected_label, expected_response (optional), severity_tag (optional).
- For classification tasks please ensure expected_label values are canonical (e.g., ESCALATE, FAQ, BILLING, TECH_SUPPORT).
- If you want to surface false-positive rate on ESCALATE, add a column called gold_escalate (0/1).

Scoring & metrics:
- Intent accuracy = (correct_labels / total). We also compute per-class precision/recall and macro-F1.
- Response quality: automated ROUGE-L + a small human evaluation (N=200) for nuanced outputs. We'll report exact thresholds and confidence intervals in the dashboard.
- Regression checks: we run a diff against your baseline run (if you provide historical outputs) and flag tokens/phrases with >X% quality drop.

Security/Isolation:
- Eval runs for customers with Dedicated purchases are executed in tenant-isolated Dedicated pools. Datasets and KV caches are purged after 30 days by default; we can shorten retention to 7 days for procurement.
- We can provide an evidence bundle (SOC2 section + config extract) and a short runbook for audit.

Run config options (what we'll set if you don't specify):
- seed: 42, max_tokens: 256, top_p: 0.9, temp: 0.0 for deterministic classification.
- batching: auto (we'll tune for p95 latency target).

Deliverables:
- Eval results dashboard link (shared), per-model CSV with predicted labels/responses, a short executive summary, and recommended model for production rollout.

Attachments: redwood_eval_template.md (dataset + scoring), small scoring script stub.

Let me know a preferred 20-min slot and we'll schedule — I can join Mon 10/19 09:00–11:00 PDT.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
